title: Saving a scene file that is read-only behaves incorrectly
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible as of Godot 4.5.1 stable, has happened significantly longer.

### System information

Godot v4.5.1.stable.mono - Fedora Linux 42 (Workstation Edition) on Wayland - X11 display driver, Single-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 980 Ti (nvidia; 580.105.08) - AMD Ryzen 7 2700X Eight-Core Processor (16 threads) - 15.55 GiB memory

### Issue description

On Linux, if a scene file is missing write permissions and an attempt to save the scene is made, it silently enables the write permission and saves the file anyway. On Windows, I remember it throwing errors while attempting to open the files, but I have only tested Linux right now.

This is poor behavior since disabling write permission is often used in locking version control, which is particularly appealing when it comes to non-code assets such as scenes. (Requiring file locks is at least more appealing than trying to teach artists about merge conflicts...) The silent changing of write permissions completely breaks the promises made by locking version control systems.

More appropriate behavior may be an optional warning when the scene is opened and an error when a save attempt is made.

### Steps to reproduce

- Create scene file, let's call it `scene.tscn`.
- (optional) Close Godot to avoid any retained state (has no effect that I can tell).
- `chmod 444 scene.tscn`, observe that all groups lack write permission.
- Open, modify, and save the scene.
- View the scene's permission bits (by `ls -l` or by other means). The write bit is now turned on for the file's owner.
